chapter: Building McShann's big band and blues records
title: Walter Brown's background and flat blues singing
summary: Walter Brown came from a CCC camp near Topeka; Dance finds his singing deadpan.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, where did Walter Brown come from?
He had been in a CC camp up around Topeka somewhere.
Well, that was like one of those Federal Government projects where they --
Guys who couldn't find a job probably had these camps and things, for them, you know.
Well, what age guy was he when you got him?

He was a grown man, that's all I can say, I never knew too much about Brown. I didn't know where he came from, or even where he passed away. But I'd say he should have been a year, maybe two years older than Bird.

Well, I mean, it's a very strange thing to me that, you know, he seems like a number of very popular blues singers who when you listen to their records, they don't really have much expression. They're almost sort of singing deadpan. You know, there's no sort of real emotion in it. The words tell the story, and he more or less sings the same melody in everything he does.
To me it's a little like rock today.
* The Creative Conservation Commission was a New Deal program of the 1930s.
